key_insight: SLiR turns activation-function verification into a general, optimizable linear-relaxation problem by computing sound bounds through slope selection and shifting.
engineering_relevance: This makes formal verification more scalable for modern neural networks because new activation functions can be supported with far less hand-crafted effort.
method: Compute the offset via a shifting procedure that preserves sound bounds over the input domain.
Require only a Lipschitz constant or a set of critical points, making the approach broadly applicable.
evidence_signal: Experiments in the abstract report tight relaxations across many practical activations and up to 7.8x more verified properties than state-of-the-art methods.
watch_item: The method’s correctness and tightness depend on choosing valid slopes and a reliable shifting procedure, so implementation details matter for sound verification.
paper_title: Shifting-based Optimizable Linear Relaxations for General Activation Functions
